open_points.subject: owner authentication
open_points.text: “Every request on either is authenticated; anything not authenticated is refused” and “The owner signs in to the owner interface with the owner credential and gets a protected session”
open_points.question: What action accepts an unauthenticated sign-in request, what does a successful sign-in return or establish, and what observable failure is returned for a wrong credential?
options: Treat sign-in as the sole unauthenticated endpoint
Require authentication outside Registry before any owner-interface request
Define sign-in as an authenticated operation using the credential on that request
open_points.default_guess: Treat sign-in as the sole unauthenticated endpoint, establish the protected owner session, and return a generic authentication failure without revealing why it failed.

open_points.subject: test-instance imports
open_points.text: “nothing moves between an instance and production except by an explicit import” versus “The only source is the Registry on the VPS, imported once” and “The local instance and the test rig are not sources”
open_points.question: Can any test instance ever be an explicit import source for production, or is the one VPS migration the only permitted production import?
options: Only the one VPS migration is permitted
Test instances may also be explicitly imported
The statement concerns movement out of production, not import into it
open_points.default_guess: Only the one VPS migration is permitted; test instances can never import into production.

open_points.subject: artifact pointers exposed to agents
open_points.text: “sees each through a minimal projection” containing “artifact pointers” and “The pointer names its owner service, which is the authority for the artifact itself”
open_points.question: Are `uri` and `payload_ref` merely non-secret identifiers, or can either act as a capability that lets the agent or its external AI provider retrieve the service-owned artifact; if retrieval is possible, which boundary prevents access to personal data?
options: Pointers are non-dereferenceable identifiers for agents
Pointers may be resolved only after authenticating separately to the owner service
Pointers are bearer capabilities and therefore must not enter the agent projection
open_points.default_guess: Treat pointers as non-secret references that confer no access; the owner service independently authenticates every retrieval.

open_points.subject: personal data in writer-controlled free text
open_points.text: “No `personal_data` value reaches it” versus “a value that breaks it is not refused and does reach the agent” and “The rule closes the path by which a `personal_data` value would reach an agent”
open_points.question: Does Registry guarantee that no actual personal data reaches an agent, or only that fields classified by Registry as `personal_data` are withheld even though aliases, room names and pointer values may contain personal data?
options: Guarantee only field-based classification
Validate or redact writer-controlled text before agent disclosure
Accept that the categorical no-personal-data guarantee has exceptions
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the enforceable guarantee as field-based only and rewrite the categorical promise so it does not claim protection against misused free-text fields.

open_points.subject: legacy free text imported into agent-visible fields
open_points.text: “with their customers, objects, rooms and pointers (ids kept), links intact” together with “Room names and artifact pointers stay in it” and the rule that writers use no names or addresses
open_points.question: Before imported rooms and pointer values can enter an agent projection, must the owner review or replace legacy values that were created before the writer rule existed?
options: Require review and sanitisation during import
Import unchanged but withhold legacy room and pointer values from agents
Import unchanged and accept that legacy personal text may reach agents
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to review and sanitise every imported agent-visible room name, alias, `uri`, `payload_ref` and digest before completing the import.

open_points.subject: customer erasure contents
open_points.text: “name, phone, e-mail and language are gone” versus “the Customer keeps its identity and the fact that it was erased, and projects keep naming it” and “nothing else”
open_points.question: When customer contact data is erased, are kind, tax id, legal name, restriction state and relationship-end date also removed, or do any of them survive?
options: Keep only `customer_ref` and the erased fact
Erase contact and fiscal values but retain lifecycle flags
Erase only the four named contact fields and retain fiscal data and other state
open_points.default_guess: Keep only `customer_ref` and the erased fact; remove kind, all contact and fiscal values, restriction state and relationship-end date.

open_points.subject: billing-data ordinary name
open_points.text: “never its contact data, the ordinary name included” versus “name, phone, e-mail and language are all the customer's contact data” and “contact data still reaches the owner alone”
open_points.question: Does the billing-data read return the customer's ordinary name to PresuPro, or is that name excluded along with all other contact data?
options: Exclude the ordinary name
Return the ordinary name despite classifying it as contact data
Return it only when it equals the recorded legal name
open_points.default_guess: Exclude the ordinary name and return only kind, tax id and legal name.

open_points.subject: revision checks on non-correction changes
open_points.text: “Every change carries CSRF protection and is validated on the server; a change made against an older revision is refused” and “A project, a customer and an object carry a revision that every accepted change moves”
open_points.question: Must archive, customer erasure, restriction changes, relationship end/resume and archived-project erasure state an expected revision and fail when stale, and what revision does each successful action return?
options: Apply revision checks to every project or customer mutation
Apply revision checks only to correction actions
Apply checks to owner-interface forms but not equivalent service operations
open_points.default_guess: Require the current revision for every mutation of a project or customer and return the resulting revision; idempotent no-ops return the unchanged revision.

open_points.subject: duplicate agent-session registration
open_points.text: “the session Registry knows, with no granted project” versus “registering a session already registered returns it unchanged”
open_points.question: What does registration return when the session already exists and already has grants, an active project or a pending request?
options: Return the existing session unchanged with all access state
Return only registration identity while preserving hidden access state
Clear the existing access state and return an empty session
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing session unchanged, including its existing grants, active project and pending-request state.

open_points.subject: session access version
open_points.text: “the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version”
open_points.question: Which actions change the access version, what is its initial value, and do idempotent grants, replacement requests, declines, active-project changes and no-op revocations advance it?
options: Advance it on every accepted access-state mutation
Advance it only when the observable access answer changes
Use it only for grant and revocation changes
open_points.default_guess: Start at 1 on registration and advance it exactly when any field returned by the access read changes.

open_points.subject: granting through an access-request answer
open_points.text: “granting adds the project the owner picks from the catalogue to the session's set” while “grant a project to an agent session” refuses an “unknown or archived project” but “answer an access request” lists only “a request no longer pending” as failure
open_points.question: When answering a pending request with a grant, what happens if the selected project is unknown, archived, anonymised or already granted, and is the pending request cleared when that grant fails?
options: Apply all grant preconditions atomically and retain the request on failure
Apply all grant preconditions but clear the request even on failure
Let the answer action grant projects that the direct grant action would refuse
open_points.default_guess: Apply the direct-grant preconditions atomically; on failure change neither access nor the pending request, while an already-granted active project is an idempotent success.

open_points.subject: display names during import
open_points.text: “each with a new display name and alias when the owner gives them” and “the owner may give each a new display name” versus “Projects imported under a person's name … are renamed in the import itself”
open_points.question: Is a new display name mandatory for every imported project, mandatory only when the legacy name identifies a person, or always optional?
options: Require a new display name for every imported project
Require it only for legacy names that violate the naming rule
Always allow the legacy display name to remain
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to provide a compliant display name for every imported project; keep the alias optional.

open_points.subject: audit event coverage
open_points.text: “significant changes of state” and “changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations” versus “Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows are not recorded”
open_points.question: For every primary action, which accepted and refused outcomes produce an audit entry—especially room creation, pointer publication or withdrawal, session registration, pending requests, request answers, active-project changes, relationship end/resume and imports—and does “agent calls” exclude state-changing agent calls?
options: Audit every accepted state-changing primary action and selected refused security events
Audit only the categories literally enumerated in R0-58
Audit owner actions but no action made with agent authority
open_points.default_guess: Audit every accepted state-changing primary action, including state-changing agent-authority calls, but not reads or refused ordinary calls.

open_points.subject: audit erasure cutoff
open_points.text: “every entry older than the date the owner gives is gone; the erasure leaves an entry of its own naming the date”
open_points.question: May the owner give today or a future date, and if so does the newly created erasure entry survive even when its timestamp is older than the supplied cutoff?
options: Reject any cutoff later than today and always retain the new erasure entry
Allow any cutoff but exempt the new entry from that erasure
Apply the cutoff after writing the new entry, which may erase the operation's own entry
open_points.default_guess: Reject a cutoff later than today, delete qualifying prior entries atomically, and then write an erasure entry that always survives.

open_points.subject: audit subject identifiers
open_points.text: “the project or customer” and “The log holds no personal value” together with “a project's id is not anonymous by itself”
open_points.question: How can an audit entry identify the affected project or customer while containing no personal value: does it store their ordinary identifiers, a non-reversible audit identifier, or only an entity type without a record reference?
options: Store ordinary ids and classify them as non-personal business-confidential data
Store separate non-reversible audit identifiers
Store no record-level identifier
open_points.default_guess: Store ordinary opaque ids as business-confidential references, but explicitly limit “no personal value” to names, addresses, contact and fiscal values.
